description: ``write_guard`` had no matcher for ``chmod`` / ``chown`` / ``chgrp``, so a permission or ownership change on a hook -- the quietest way to silence it, since the file stays in place unreadable and nothing reports it -- was allowed on Bash while ``cp evil.json .claude/settings.json`` denied on the same tree (DEF-638, driven at HEAD). The verb roster in ``tests/test_speedbump_irreversible.py`` had carried both verbs for months with no pattern behind either. Fix: ``_CHMOD_CHOWN_RE`` (command-position anchored, ``#`` ends the span) feeds every non-flag operand after the mode/owner -- all of them under ``--reference=`` -- through ``_is_protected`` via ``_permission_targets``; the three verbs joined ``_NON_REPARSING_HEADS`` so a quoted separator decoy is neutralised before the span is read, and operands are quote-aware so a path with a space is one target. Extended 2026-09-05 (DEF-695) to ``chflags`` (the macOS-native silencer: ``uchg`` is immutable AND undeletable), ``chattr`` and ``setfacl``, all three allowed beside a denied ``chmod 000`` at filing; ``setfacl`` takes every positional (its ACL spec rides on a flag and ``-b``/``-k`` carry none), the others skip the mode/flags token. The same no-mode shape exists inside ``chmod`` itself on macOS: ``chmod -E <file>`` applies an ACL read from stdin (a deny ACE makes a hook unreadable) and ``-N``/``-I`` strip or inherit one; every positional is a file under those flags. Extended 2026-09-07 (DEF-697) to the PowerShell tool, where the Windows twins -- ``icacls <hook> /deny Everyone:(R)``, ``attrib +R <hook>``, ``Set-Acl -Path <hook> -AclObject $acl`` and ``Set-ItemProperty -Path <hook> -Name IsReadOnly -Value $true`` -- all allowed beside a denied ``Set-Content <hook>`` on the same leg (driven at HEAD, filed by the DEF-695 failure-mode pass). ``_PS_PERMISSION_RE`` is anchored on ``_PS_CMD_POS`` and ``_ps_permission_targets`` applies a per-verb rule: the two Win32 tools are slash-switched with the path first (``icacls``) or among ``+``/``-`` attribute tokens (``attrib``) and their bare forms DISPLAY, so those are reads; the two cmdlets are always writes and every non-switch operand is a candidate, a colon-bound ``-Path:`` value included.
